title: Work, jobs and the progressive
objectives: I can talk about my job, my workplace and my schedule.
I can say what is happening right now with estar plus the gerund, and tell it apart from a habit in the simple present.
I can use ficar in its main meanings: stay, become, be located and ficar sabendo.
I can handle a simple phone call and a work message using phrases such as alô, quem fala, um momento and vou transferir.

grammar.title: The present progressive: estar plus gerund
grammar.explanation:
To say what is happening right now, use the present of estar plus the gerund. The gerund is formed from the infinitive: -ar verbs change to -ando, -er verbs to -endo and -ir verbs to -indo. So falar becomes falando, comer becomes comendo and abrir becomes abrindo. Estou falando, ela está comendo, eles estão abrindo.

Most verbs are regular, including the ones that look odd, such as fazer (fazendo), dizer (dizendo), ler (lendo), ir (indo) and vir (vindo). The one real irregular gerund in everyday use is pôr, which becomes pondo. In Portuguese the gerund always ends in -ndo and never changes for gender or number.

Brazilian Portuguese always uses the gerund here, never a plus infinitive. Estou a fazer belongs to European Portuguese and sounds odd in Brazil. In casual speech estou becomes tô and está becomes tá: Tô saindo agora, Tá chovendo. An object pronoun usually goes between estar and the gerund in speech: Estou te esperando, Ela está me ligando.

examples.en: Right now I am writing an email.

grammar.title: Present versus progressive
grammar.explanation:
The simple present describes habits, routines, general facts and situations that are stable: Eu trabalho num banco, Ela chega às oito, A loja abre às nove. The progressive describes what is in progress right now or around now, especially if it is temporary or different from usual: Hoje estou trabalhando em casa, Ela está estudando para a prova.

Two differences from English matter. First, the progressive is not normally used for the future: English says I am leaving tomorrow, but Portuguese says Viajo amanhã or Vou viajar amanhã. Second, estar plus gerund with ir and vir is very common for immediate movement: Estou indo means I am on my way, and Estou chegando means I am almost there.

The simple present is also fine for right now when the verb is naturally stable, such as gostar, saber, querer and ter. People do not say estou querendo in ordinary use. Markers like normalmente, sempre and todo dia point to the simple present; agora, neste momento, hoje and esta semana often point to the progressive.

grammar.title: Ficar: stay, become, be located, ficar sabendo
grammar.explanation:
Ficar is one of the most useful verbs in Brazilian Portuguese. Its basic meaning is to stay: Vou ficar em casa hoje. It is also the everyday verb for the location of things that do not move, like buildings and streets: O banco fica perto do metrô. In this sense it replaces estar and is more natural than ser.

Ficar plus an adjective means to become or to get: ficar nervoso, ficar cansado, ficar feliz. It describes a change: Fiquei nervosa na entrevista, meaning I got nervous. Ficar plus com means to keep, and ficar plus de plus infinitive means to be supposed to do something, as in Fiquei de ligar.

Ficar sabendo means to find out or to hear about something, especially indirectly: Fiquei sabendo da vaga por uma amiga. Note that the preterite fiquei is used because finding out is a single event. Do not confuse the forms: the preterite of ficar is fiquei, ficou, ficamos, ficaram; the present is fico, fica, ficamos, ficam.

grammar.title: Time expressions and phone phrases
grammar.explanation:
Agora means now and neste momento means at this moment, both pairing well with the progressive. Atualmente means currently, at this time, and is a false friend of actually; the Portuguese for actually is na verdade. Ainda means still (Ainda estou trabalhando) or yet with a negative (Ainda não terminei, I haven't finished yet). Já means already (Já terminei) and, in questions, ever or yet (Você já almoçou?).

On the phone, Brazilians answer with Alô or with the name of the company. To ask who is calling, say Quem fala? or Com quem eu falo? In offices you will also hear É da parte de quem? Other polite phrases are Um momento, por favor, Vou transferir a ligação, A linha está ocupada, Ele não está no momento and Quer deixar um recado? If the line is bad or drops, say A ligação caiu or Não estou ouvindo bem.

For messages, Brazilians write Tô chegando, Já vi, Depois eu respondo and Me avisa. Replying with an áudio (voice message) is very common, even at work.

culture.title: WhatsApp, working hours and phone manners
culture.text:
WhatsApp is the main way Brazilians communicate, and it has moved into the workplace: companies, teams and even clients have groups, and quick decisions are made by message or by áudio. Many people do not like typing and send long voice messages instead, often with a quick Oi, tudo bem? at the start. Messages like Tô chegando (I am arriving) or Já vi (I already saw it) are extremely common, and Tô chegando does not always mean the person is nearly there.

The standard working day is usually eight hours, with a lunch break known as horário de almoço, and the official term for a regular job is emprego com carteira assinada, meaning the employer has signed the work card and the employee gets benefits. Formal employees typically receive a 13th salary in December and thirty days of vacation a year. On the phone, people answer with Alô or the company name and use senhor and senhora with strangers. It is polite to ask É da parte de quem?, listen to the answer and then say Um momento, por favor.

readings.title: Um dia diferente para a Renata

paragraphs.pt: Renata é engenheira e trabalha numa empresa de São Paulo. Normalmente, ela chega ao escritório às oito e sai às cinco.
paragraphs.en: Renata is an engineer and works for a company in São Paulo. Normally she arrives at the office at eight and leaves at five.

paragraphs.pt: Hoje o dia está diferente. Está chovendo muito, e por isso ela está trabalhando de casa.
paragraphs.en: Today the day is different. It is raining a lot, so she is working from home.

paragraphs.pt: Neste momento, Renata está participando de uma reunião por vídeo. Os colegas estão falando sobre um projeto novo, e o chefe está perguntando sobre o prazo.
paragraphs.en: At this moment, Renata is taking part in a video meeting. Her colleagues are talking about a new project, and the boss is asking about the deadline.

paragraphs.pt: Atualmente, a empresa está contratando mais engenheiros, e Renata está ajudando nas entrevistas. Hoje ela ficou sabendo que já há cinco candidatos.
paragraphs.en: Currently, the company is hiring more engineers, and Renata is helping with the interviews. Today she found out that there are already five candidates.

paragraphs.pt: Ela ainda não almoçou. Às duas horas, finalmente, Renata faz uma pausa e come alguma coisa. Ela gosta de trabalhar em casa, mas prefere o escritório.
paragraphs.en: She has not had lunch yet. At two o'clock, finally, Renata takes a break and eats something. She likes working from home, but prefers the office.
